title: Local projective reconstruction of driven bosonic Hamiltonians
summary: Inferring a Hamiltonian from a single quantum trajectory is generally non-unique. This ambiguity limits inverse use of projective quantum geometry. Here we show that a nearest-neighbour structural prior makes the problem locally identifiable. For a smooth real time-dependent Jacobi Hamiltonian initialized at a ladder endpoint, the physical-time projective jet through order M+1 reconstructs the first M couplings, their logarithmic rates, and diagonal energy differences, up to an overall scalar-energy gauge.
